slate-1.purpose: Page background, resting tile fill, the fill behind the translucent topbar and drawer, the podcast mark's glyph colour, the bullet-thread dot centre.

slate-2.purpose: One tonal step up, never more — palette shell, dropdown, tile hover, entry hover bleed, primary button's resting field, dev pre fallback.

slate-3.purpose: Secondary button, nav hover, inline code, keyboard caps, theme-toggle track, copy-code button.

slate-4.purpose: Secondary button hover, dev pre fallback border, webmention avatar placeholder.

slate-5.purpose: The heavier 1px — link underlines, palette panel border and internal divisions, kbd outlines, post-footer and related-posts rules, theme toggle's selected pill, Markdown-actions border. Used where a line must read as an edge rather than a divider.

slate-6.purpose: The universal separator and the most structurally load-bearing colour in the system. Chosen by measurement: 1.37:1 light and 1.65:1 dark against the ground, where slate-4 measured 1.19 / 1.31 and disappeared.

slate-7.purpose: Resting heading anchor, resting drawer chevron.

slate-8.purpose: Palette placeholder, the # before a tag, the resting entry arrow, the brand-lockup slash, the scrollbar thumb.

slate-10.purpose: Monospace metadata not carrying primary information — tile footers, chips, back links, section actions, source notes, palette hints.

slate-11.purpose: All body copy, secondary text, prose paragraphs, entry excerpts, and the mono facts under a title. Numerically the most-used token in the codebase.

slate-12.purpose: Headings, entry and tile titles, and any text that must win a scan.

ruby-3.purpose: The primary button's hover fill, the active drawer item, the accent callout background. The nearest thing to a ruby surface on the site, and it exists only as a hover or a current state.

ruby-8.purpose: The theme toggle's inset focus ring, used because its buttons sit flush inside a track where a 2px offset outline would clip.

ruby-9.purpose: The focus ring, and the primary button's resting border at 50% opacity. The only fully saturated step in use, and it appears only as a 2px line. Identical in both themes — the one token that does not flip.

ruby-11.purpose: The accent, and the only one. Every hover, the active-tab underline, the current contents entry, the primary button's label, the blockquote rule, the bullet-thread dot ring, the text caret.

ruby-12.purpose: Text on ruby-tinted surfaces — ::selection, the accent callout, the accent heading scheme.

amber-500.purpose: The stale-post notice only — /30 border on a /5 wash with a solid-amber icon, raised on posts over two years past their last update. A borrowed semantic rather than borrowed data: 'this may be out of date' is a caution the brand red would misreport, so the convention is borrowed instead of invented. NOTE: this is Tailwind's own amber-500, not the four-step Radix amber subset bridged in @theme (--color-amber-3/-6/-9/-11), which nothing currently references. The bridge is unused and the Tailwind value does not flip between themes.

dataColors.name: language-dot
dataColors.value: GitHub's own language colour, per repository
dataColors.purpose: The 8px dot on a project tile's fact row. Not a choice the site makes — the ecosystem already assigns it, so Ruby reads as Ruby. Accepted plainly, never re-mapped into the palette.

dataColors.name: podcast-hue
dataColors.constraint: Lightness (0.62) and chroma (0.14) are fixed; hue is the only free variable. This is what keeps a column of shows reading as one family rather than as five unrelated colours.
dataColors.purpose: The 56px rounded mark on a podcast row; an inactive show drops to opacity 0.7. A FALLBACK identity, not a primary one — every show in the data carries real artwork that covers the mark, so the generated hue surfaces only for a show with no image or one whose image fails to load.

display.purpose: The homepage h1 only. Sub-solid leading and tight tracking make a two-word name read as a mark. Capped at 680px and balanced.

page-title.purpose: Index and listing page titles. A listing is a room, not an argument.

h2.purpose: Section headings inside the reading column. They must outrank the prose by an obvious step — at 17px against 17px body the sections read flat.

h3.purpose: Sub-headings inside the reading column. An h3 below body size is a heading that loses to its own paragraph.

read.purpose: The reading column and nothing else. Source Serif 4 at a 65ch measure, chosen in-browser against real character width at this size.

title.purpose: The largest type inside a list — the year marker over an archive group.

lede.purpose: Hero standfirst and page descriptions. One step above interface body and deliberately tighter than the serif column it must not imitate.

row.purpose: Every entry and tile title, the palette input, the topbar wordmark. Close to body size on purpose — a list is scanned as a body of work, not a stack of headlines.

body.purpose: The global default on <body>. Interface copy, drawer items.

note.purpose: Excerpts, descriptions, section descriptions, contents entries, button labels.

code.purpose: Fenced code blocks. Set below the 18px reading column on purpose — a wide sample has to fit the measure without horizontal scroll before it has to match the text.

label.purpose: Section labels in the rail and the contents heading. The signature type treatment of the site: 12px mono uppercase, 0.08em, slate-11, on a hairline.

meta.purpose: Dates, reading times, durations, tags, counts, keyboard caps, footer, post navigation. font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums is set globally on .font-mono so numerals align in a column.

shadows.name: popover
shadows.purpose: The Markdown-actions dropdown on a post — the only non-modal popover on the site, and the only shadow inside the reading column.

shadows.name: selected-control
shadows.purpose: The selected pill in the theme toggle, so the chosen mode reads as pressed inside its track.

shadows.name: framed-image
shadows.purpose: The Image component's figure variant, where a slate hairline alone would disappear into the ground the image sits on.

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: Everything else, deliberately — including the command palette and the mobile drawer. Elevation comes from the border and the field; the 1px slate-6 hairline is the only separator for anything that scrolls with the page.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: The workhorse. Nearly every hover, focus, and current-state change in the system.

motion.name: ease-authored
motion.purpose: The one authored motion moment: the command palette panel's 180ms drop from translateY(-10px).

motion.name: drawer
motion.purpose: The mobile drawer and its scrim — opacity plus an 8px translate.

motion.name: view-transition
motion.purpose: Cross-document root fade, armed by <meta name="view-transition" content="same-origin"> in the root layout. Without the meta tag Turbo Drive handles the navigation and the @view-transition rule is dead code.

motion.name: nudge
motion.purpose: Section-action and primary-button icons right, the back arrow left.

motion.name: arrival
motion.purpose: The entry row's trailing arrow, revealed on group-hover and group-focus-visible. At rest it repeated down forty-five rows carrying no information.

motion.name: reduced
motion.purpose: The prefers-reduced-motion floor, applied to every animation, transition, and scroll behaviour — then repeated for ::view-transition-old(root) / ::view-transition-new(root) by name, because * does not match pseudo-elements and the cross-document fade would otherwise outlive the blanket rule.

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: Named in @theme. The @handle, the 'Search' word and the ⌘K cap drop; header height goes 64px to 56px.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Tailwind default. Full and media entry densities collapse to one column.

breakpoints.name: card-grid
breakpoints.purpose: A bare media query in index.css — the tile grid goes from two columns to one.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Tailwind default. Compact entries collapse to one column; page gutters drop from 36px to 16px; tile padding drops to 14px vertical with no horizontal padding.

breakpoints.name: nav
breakpoints.purpose: Named in @theme. Primary nav collapses to the hamburger; the hero, the label rail, and the reading rail all unstack. The single most load-bearing breakpoint in the system.

measures.name: reading
measures.purpose: The article column. Measured in-browser against real character width.

measures.name: shell-wide
measures.purpose: Homepage, listings, topbar, and footer — all three repeat this measure so they align to the same edge.

measures.name: shell-reading
measures.purpose: Post pages: wide enough to hold apparatus in the margin while the column beside it stays at a reading measure, not wide enough for the prose to grow.

focus.purpose: A system guarantee, applied once so every focusable element is covered rather than chased component by component. It sits in @layer base specifically so a component can still override it from markup — unlayered CSS outranks Tailwind's utilities whatever the specificity, so the theme toggle's inset ring and the palette's borderless input could not opt out. Inside base, a utility wins as expected.

browserSurfaces.name: theme-resolution
browserSurfaces.value: data-theme set from localStorage or prefers-color-scheme by an inline script in <head>, before first paint

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The site's one primary action. A ruby hairline with a ruby-11 label — deliberately not a ruby field. The solid fill it replaced put white on ruby-9 at 3.89:1, under the 4.5:1 its 13.5px label needs, and read as the most landing-page-shaped object on the page. This measures 5.16:1 in light and 8.36:1 in dark, and the fill still arrives on hover.

A 168px lead column of measurement — the same margin the section label hangs in — a title carrying its own facts, and a trailing arrow that arrives on hover or keyboard focus rather than repeating down forty-five rows at rest. Entirely slate until touched.

components.name: Theme Toggle
components.description: A three-way radiogroup — system, light, dark — as 32px circular buttons inside a slate-3 pill. The selected one lifts to slate-5 with a slate-12 icon and the system's one selected-control shadow, driven entirely by aria-checked so the accessible state and the visual state cannot drift apart. Focus is an inset ruby-8 ring rather than the standard offset outline, because the buttons sit flush inside a track — the exact case the base focus rule was put in @layer base to allow.

narrative.overview:
This is the familiar arrangement for a working engineer's site — a name, a standfirst, a ledger of what exists, then ruled lists of writing and open source — built at a craft level the category rarely reaches. The invention is not in the layout. It is in the focus ring you can't lose, the hover that arrives on the one element you pointed at, the row that reveals its arrow only when you're on it, and the fact that both themes are real. Convention carries the structure so that every unit of attention can be spent on state, timing, and contrast.

The ground is a Radix slate ramp, composed dark-first: dark is where the design was made and reviewed, light is a tested peer. There is exactly one accent — Radix ruby — and it is spent entirely on state: hover, focus, active, current. There is deliberately no solid ruby field at rest anywhere on the site, including the primary button, which is a ruby hairline with a ruby-11 label. Surfaces are separated by a 1px slate-6 rule and never by a shadow. Three typefaces divide the work absolutely: Archivo for chrome and lists, Source Serif 4 for the reading column and nowhere else, Geist Mono for anything that is a measurement.

The one compositional idea is the label rail: a 168px margin on the left carrying what a section is called, what it holds, and where the rest of it lives, with the column beside it carrying nothing but the work. The same 168px is the lead column of a chronological row, so a section label and the dates under it hang in the same margin. Below 820px the rail stacks, because a 168px margin is a luxury a phone does not have. This system was built code-led against the running site; there are no comps, and nothing here is derived from a design file.

The confirmed anti-reference is the landing page: a solid accent field as a first object, a card grid used as the default primitive, a small coloured line above a title, decorated section headings. Each of those was present at some point in the build and was removed by measurement.
keyCharacteristics: One ground (Radix slate, all 12 steps) and one accent (Radix ruby, spent only on state). Every other colour arrives by one of three narrow routes — a borrowed semantic (amber, staleness only), upstream data (GitHub's language colours), or a one-axis derived fallback (the podcast hue).
Every ramp step is redefined per [data-theme], so the token value flips rather than the class — markup carries almost no dark: variants.
Three faces with strictly divided jobs: Archivo (chrome, lists, display), Source Serif 4 (the reading column only), Geist Mono (dates, counts, durations, tags, code, labels).
Fifteen named type roles in @theme, each carrying its own leading, tracking, and weight, so text-meta is the whole decision.
Two layout primitives carry nearly the whole site: Entry (one chronological row, three densities) and Tile (one grid cell for peers).
A 1px slate-6 hairline is the only separator for anything that scrolls with the page.
Focus is a single base-layer rule over every focusable element, so it cannot be forgotten per component.
Links are underlined, not coloured — ruby against body slate measured 1.09:1 and colour alone was not a distinction.

rules.name: The Accent-Is-State Rule
rules.body: Ruby marks what is hovered, focused, active, or current — and nothing else. There is deliberately no solid ruby field at rest anywhere on the site. The primary button proves the rule rather than excepting it: the solid fill it replaced put white on ruby-9 at 3.89:1, under the 4.5:1 its 13.5px label needs, and read as the most landing-page-shaped object on the page. The hairline version measures 5.16:1 in light and 8.36:1 in dark, and the fill still arrives on hover. At rest a full viewport should hold almost no ruby at all — often only the period after the wordmark and one active nav underline.

rules.name: The Upstream-Colour Rule
rules.body: A colour outside slate and ruby is admissible when it is data the site did not author. GitHub's language colour on a project tile is the case: Ruby reading red is information the ecosystem already assigns, and the dot reports it rather than deciding it. Accept it plainly — no caveat, no re-mapping into the palette, no "brand-safe" substitute, because a substituted language colour is simply wrong. Amber for staleness is the one borrowed semantic rather than borrowed data: "may be out of date" is a caution the brand red would misreport, so the convention is borrowed instead of invented.

rules.name: The Derived-Identifier Rule
rules.body: A colour may be generated only when the generation is constrained to one axis and the result is a fallback. The podcast mark is oklch(0.62 0.14 <hue>) with accent_hue supplied per show: lightness and chroma are fixed and hue is the only free variable, which is the entire reason a column of shows reads as one family rather than as five unrelated colours. It is also a fallback identity, not a primary one — every show in the data carries real artwork that covers the mark, so the generated hue surfaces only for a show with no image. Widen the generation to lightness or chroma and you have invented a palette; use it where artwork exists and you have invented decoration. Neither this rule nor the one above is licence to invent a decorative colour: if a new colour cannot answer "what fact does this encode?", it does not go in.

rules.name: The Dark-First Rule
rules.body: Both themes ship and both must be legible, but dark is the composed ground and light is the tested peer. The mechanism is why the system stays small: because every ramp step is redefined inside [data-theme="dark"], the token value flips rather than the class, so text-slate-11 is correct in both themes and markup needs almost no dark: variants. Author a new colour as a light/dark pair in frontend/styles/index.css and the rest is free.

rules.name: The Bridge Rule
rules.body: A Radix step is usable in markup only if it has been bridged into @theme as --color-<name>. An unbridged utility produces silence, not an error — the class does nothing and the element falls back to inherited colour. Slate and ruby are bridged in full precisely so a step is never referenced before it exists; amber is a deliberate four-step subset. Add the bridge and the usage in the same change.

rules.name: The Named-Role Rule
rules.body: Every size on the site is one of the fifteen roles in @theme. Never write a raw text-[15px], never pair a role with a competing leading-*/tracking-*/font-* unless the override is the point, and if a new size is genuinely needed, add a role with all four properties rather than assembling one at a call site. The only sanctioned exception is a glyph inside a mark, where the size is artwork.

rules.name: The Three-Voices Rule
rules.body: Chrome, lists, and display are Archivo. The reading column is Source Serif 4 and nothing else is. Anything that is a measurement — a date, a count, a duration, a tag, a keyboard cap, a code span, a section label — is Geist Mono. There is no fourth category and no overlap: if a small line is a sentence rather than a measurement, it is sans, even at 13.5px in a margin.

rules.name: The Underline Rule
rules.body: Links in the reading column are underlined, not coloured. Ruby-11 against body slate measures 1.09:1 in light and 1.01:1 in dark, so colour alone was not a distinction at all — WCAG 1.4.1 wants 3:1 for a colour-only difference. The underline is the affordance and the colour is only reinforcement: decoration-ruby-11/40 at rest going solid on hover, over a global text-underline-offset: 0.2em.

rules.name: The No-Kicker Rule
rules.body: No kicker, ever. A small accent line above a title is an eyebrow. It existed as an Entry parameter and was deleted: the show, the venue, the episode number and the city are facts about the item, not headings over it, and they live in the meta row with the other facts.

rules.name: The Label-Not-Title Rule
rules.body: Section labels are never large. `now`, `featured work`, `recent posts`, `Talks` are 12px mono uppercase 0.08em in slate-11, hanging in the rail above a hairline — a filing tab, not a banner. Hierarchy is carried by the ruled structure and by which face is used, not by making headings big.

rules.name: The Rows-for-Chronology Rule
rules.body: Dated content is an Entry — posts, talks, episodes, CFPs, appearances, shows. Genuinely parallel items with no meaningful order may Tile — projects, featured work. A grid never carries dated content. This is why writing, speaking, and podcasting read as one body of work rather than four lists that merely resemble each other, and it is the reason a card grid is not the site's default primitive.

rules.name: The Label-Rail Rule
rules.body: Apparatus goes in the margin; the column carries the work. What a section is called, what it holds, where the rest of it lives, when a post was written, how long it takes, what is in it — all of that hangs in a 168px (or 208px) left rail, and it stacks rather than shrinks below nav. Never inline apparatus into the content column on desktop, and never open a second rail inside a rail: the archive's year marker sits at the left edge sharing a column with the dates below it, because giving it its own 168px column stacked two margins and opened a gap down the middle of the page.

rules.name: The One-Column Rule
rules.body: Content is a single centred column at every width. No sidebar, no asymmetric listing page, no two-up article layout. The homepage hero is the single sanctioned exception: it may pair a prose column with one narrow derived ledger, collapsing to stacked at nav.

rules.name: The Hairline-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: When two regions need separating, the answer is a 1px slate-6 line. If an element scrolls with the document, it is flat — no exceptions, including tiles, rows, sections, and the reading rail. A shadow is admissible only on a genuine popover or a selected control, and even a modal here does without one.

rules.name: The Square-Content Rule
rules.body: Anything that scrolls with the page and is separated by a hairline is square. Radius is for controls, chips, and things that float.

rules.name: The Focus-Guarantee Rule
rules.body: Keyboard focus is a system guarantee, not a per-component decision: one rule over :where(a, button, input, select, textarea, summary, [tabindex]):focus-visible gives every focusable element a 2px solid ruby-9 outline at 2px offset with a 4px radius. It lives in @layer base specifically so a component can still override it from markup — unlayered CSS outranks Tailwind's utilities whatever the specificity, so the theme toggle's inset ring and the palette's borderless input could not opt out. Inside base, a utility wins as expected. Never remove focus from a control; override the indicator if you must, and never chase focus component by component.

rules.name: The Inert-Until-Touched Rule
rules.body: Components have no colour, border, shadow, or decoration at rest beyond their hairline. Everything expressive — the ruby, the arrow, the tonal shift — is a hover, focus, or current state. A screenshot of this site at rest should look almost dead; using it should not.

rules.name: The Whole-Row Rule
rules.body: When a row or tile is a link, the entire region is the anchor and the entire region responds. Never a small "read more" inside an inert block. The one sanctioned alternative is an inert row that names several destinations as links, which is what a talk with both a video and slides gets.

rules.name: The Derived-Number Rule
rules.body: Any number the design displays must be derived from the collections or data at build time. The homepage ledger counts posts, repos, and talks from the resources themselves; the one constant, Remote Ruby's back catalogue, is stated conservatively as 350+ because the data file carries only the latest episode. A count that can go stale silently is worse than no count.

dos: Do reach for Entry for anything dated and Tile for anything genuinely parallel, and write a thin adapter component that maps your data onto one of them rather than a new primitive.
Do hang apparatus in the 168px label rail — the section name, its one-line description, its "everything else" link — and leave the column beside it carrying only the work.
Do spend ruby only on hover, focus, active, and current. The resting page should hold almost no ruby.
Do use one of the fifteen named type roles for every size, and add a new role with its own leading, tracking, and weight rather than assembling one at a call site.
Do put every measurement in Geist Mono, the reading column in Source Serif 4, and everything else in Archivo.
Do author every new colour as a light/dark pair in frontend/styles/index.css and bridge it into @theme as --color-<name> in the same change.
Do separate regions with a 1px slate-6 hairline, and give hover states exactly one tonal step (slate-1 → slate-2).
Do underline links in prose. Colour is reinforcement, never the distinction.
Do let the base focus rule do its job, and if a control genuinely needs a different indicator, override it from markup rather than removing it.
Do derive any number the design displays from the collections or data at build time.
donts: Don't put dated content in a grid. Chronology is rows; a grid is for peers with no meaningful order.
Don't add a solid ruby field at rest — including on the primary action. The measured fill failed contrast at 3.89:1 and read as a landing-page object; the hairline is the design, not a compromise.

Don't add a second accent. A colour outside slate and ruby is admissible only as upstream data (GitHub's language colour), a borrowed semantic (amber for staleness), or a one-axis derived fallback (the podcast hue) — never as a choice made for its own sake.
Don't generate a colour on more than one axis. The podcast hue rotates hue at fixed lightness and chroma; free a second axis and a family of shows becomes five unrelated colours.
Don't put a kicker above a title. A show, a venue, an episode number, or a city is a fact about the item and belongs in the meta row.
Don't put a shadow on anything that scrolls with the page. Even the palette and the drawer do without one; a border and a field are the elevation.
Don't round content. Entry rows, tile cells, the ledger, and ruled sections are square.
Don't make a section label large. Hierarchy comes from the rail, the rules, and the face — not from type size.
Don't reference a Radix step @theme doesn't bridge; an unbridged utility fails silently rather than erroring.
Don't open a second rail inside a rail, or inline apparatus into the content column on desktop.
Don't add a dark: variant to fix a colour. If a token looks wrong in one theme, the pair in index.css is wrong.
Don't ship a change verified in only one theme. Dark is where the work is composed; light is tested, not assumed.
Don't drift toward the landing page: no accent field as a first object, no card grid as the default primitive, no decorated section headings, no stock cover images on rows.
